items.message: The regex `_REVIEW` and `aspect_from` take only the first `\S+` token after `/review`, so a name like `../../etc/passwd` is refused because it is not in `known` — but the refusal message interpolates the raw user-supplied string with `{asked!r}`. An attacker who can comment on a pull request sends `/review <crafted string>` and controls a substring of the exception message, which is then raised as a `click.ClickException` and printed to stdout. The `options` string interpolated into refusal messages is built from `known`, which comes from `adapter.compositions()`. If that method returns labels whose string representations contain characters meaningful to whatever renders the error (e.g. HTML comment sequences like `-->`), those propagate into the refusal text. GitLab's `change_refs` calls `self._request("GET", ...)` without a try/except. Unlike the GitHub implementation, which catches `RuntimeError` from `gh pr view` and returns `None`, a GitLab API error (e.g. network failure, 404 on an issue number) will propagate as an unhandled exception rather than returning `None`.
